title: Illuminate a clear path to completion
principle: Luke Wroblewski’s public form-design teaching (lukew.com / Web Form Design talks): every form’s primary job is completion—clear scan line, pacing, visible primary action, minimized pain. AI forms often look ‘designed’ but hide the finish line.
procedure: Remove or postpone every field that isn’t required for the outcome.
Top-align labels; one primary action; demote secondary.
Show progress when multi-step; keep scope honest.
Inline validation that helps, not punishes on first focus.
Mobile: appropriate input types, targets, and keyboard-friendly actions.
examplePrompts:
Refactor this form for path-to-completion (Luke W public form practices):
- Cut/postpone nonessential fields.
- Top-aligned labels; one primary CTA.
- Inline validation after input; helpful errors.
- Mobile input types + 44px targets.
Return cut list + UI diff.
This checkout has two solid buttons—make hierarchy obvious and shorten the path.
promptWhy: Cut list is the craft; visuals alone don’t finish forms.
Names mobile input-type specifics AI skips.
tips: https://www.lukew.com/ · public PDFs/talks on web form design
